text: Earth is about 4.5 billion years old, so the core has been hot since formation
as_written: blazing hot for four and a half billion years
source: Dalrymple 1991; USGS age of the Earth, about 4.54 billion years

text: The core-mantle boundary lies about 2,890 km below the surface
as_written: Almost two thousand nine hundred kilometres beneath your boots
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model (Dziewonski and Anderson 1981)

text: The core is about a third of Earth's mass (about 32 percent)
as_written: The core holds about a third of the planet's mass
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model (Dziewonski and Anderson 1981)

text: Core radius is about 3,480 km versus Earth's 6,371 km, about 55 percent, and about 16 percent by volume
as_written: roughly sixteen percent of the planet's volume
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model (Dziewonski and Anderson 1981)

text: The inner core radius is about 1,220 km
as_written: about twelve hundred and twenty kilometres
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model; first identified by Lehmann 1936

text: Moon radius is about 1,737 km, so the inner core is about 70 percent of it
as_written: around seventy percent of the radius of the Moon
source: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter / NASA Moon fact sheet

text: The liquid outer core is about 2,260 km thick (2,890 km to 5,150 km depth)
as_written: about twenty-two hundred and sixty kilometres thick
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model (Dziewonski and Anderson 1981)

text: Inner core boundary temperature is about 6,000 K with several hundred kelvin uncertainty
as_written: about six thousand kelvin, give or take several hundred
source: Anzellini et al. 2013, Science 340, 464 (about 6,230 K plus or minus 500 K)

text: The Sun's surface temperature is about 5,772 K, comparable to the inner core boundary
as_written: comparable to the surface of the Sun
source: IAU 2015 Resolution B3, nominal solar effective temperature 5,772 K

text: Pressure at Earth's centre is about 360 gigapascals, over 3 million atmospheres
as_written: about three hundred and sixty gigapascals
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model (about 364 GPa)

text: 360 GPa is more than three million times atmospheric pressure of about 101 kPa
as_written: more than three million times the pressure of the air around you
source: Preliminary Reference Earth Model; standard atmosphere 101,325 Pa

text: The inner core grows by roughly a millimetre per year in most thermal evolution models
as_written: by about a millimetre a year in most models
source: Labrosse 2015, Physics of the Earth and Planetary Interiors 247, 36-55

text: Inner core age estimates range from roughly 0.5 to over 1 billion years
as_written: from about half a billion years to a bit over a billion
source: Bono et al. 2019, Nature Geoscience (about 565 million years); Biggin et al. 2015, Nature Geoscience (1.0 to 1.5 billion years)

text: Earth had a magnetic field at least about 3.4 to 3.5 billion years ago
as_written: about three and a half billion years ago
source: Tarduno et al. 2010, Science 327, 1238 (3.4 to 3.45 billion years)

text: Shear waves cannot travel through liquid; Oldham identified the core in 1906
as_written: In 1906 the geologist Richard Oldham spotted
source: Oldham 1906, Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society 62, 456

text: Jeffreys showed in 1926 the core is liquid
as_written: In 1926 the physicist Harold Jeffreys showed
source: Jeffreys 1926, Geophysical Supplement to the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

text: Lehmann discovered the inner core in 1936
as_written: Then in 1936 the seismologist Inge Lehmann
source: Lehmann 1936, Bureau Central Seismologique International

text: A P wave takes about 20 minutes to cross to the antipode
as_written: roughly twenty minutes to cross the whole Earth
source: IASP91 / PREM travel-time tables, IRIS

text: Decadal variations in length of day are of order a millisecond, attributed partly to core-mantle angular momentum exchange
as_written: wanders by roughly a millisecond over the course of decades
source: International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service; Gross 2015, Treatise on Geophysics

text: The dipole free decay time of the core field is of order 20,000 years, depending on iron conductivity
as_written: a leak time of roughly twenty thousand years
source: Gubbins and Herrero-Bervera, Encyclopedia of Geomagnetism and Paleomagnetism; Pozzo et al. 2012, Nature 485, 355 on conductivity uncertainty

text: The north magnetic pole has moved tens of km per year in recent decades from Canada toward Siberia
as_written: at tens of kilometres a year
source: NOAA NCEI and British Geological Survey World Magnetic Model

text: Earth's field has weakened about 9 percent over the last 200 years
as_written: about nine percent over the last two hundred years
source: ESA Swarm mission

text: Exponential decay with a 20,000 year time constant gives about 1 percent loss in 200 years
as_written: only about one percent over the same two centuries
source: Arithmetic from exp(-200/20000), using the dipole free decay time above

text: Exponential decay gives about 5 percent loss after 1,000 years
as_written: has lost about five percent
source: Arithmetic from exp(-1000/20000)

text: Exponential decay gives about 61 percent remaining after 10,000 years
as_written: about sixty percent of today's
source: Arithmetic from exp(-10000/20000)

text: About 37 percent remains after 20,000 years
as_written: After twenty thousand, about a third
source: Arithmetic from exp(-1)

text: About 13.5 percent remains after 40,000 years
as_written: roughly a seventh
source: Arithmetic from exp(-2)

text: Surface geomagnetic field strength ranges from about 25 to 65 microtesla
as_written: between about twenty-five and sixty-five microtesla
source: NOAA NCEI World Magnetic Model; International Geomagnetic Reference Field

text: Loggerhead hatchlings change swimming direction when the magnetic field is rotated
as_written: change their swimming direction when the field around them is rotated
source: Lohmann 1991, Journal of Experimental Biology 155, 37-49

text: Auroras were reported in the Caribbean during the 1859 storm
as_written: when aurora was reported in the Caribbean
source: Carrington event records; Green and Boardsen 2006, Advances in Space Research

text: Earth's total surface heat loss is about 46 terawatts
as_written: about forty-six terawatts of heat
source: Davies and Davies 2010, Solid Earth 1, 5-24

text: Core-mantle boundary heat flow is estimated at about 5 to 15 terawatts
as_written: between about five and fifteen terawatts
source: Lay, Hernlund and Buffett 2008, Nature Geoscience 1, 25-32

text: The March 13, 1989 geomagnetic storm collapsed the Hydro-Quebec grid in about 90 seconds
as_written: the grid collapsed in about ninety seconds
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation report on the March 1989 geomagnetic disturbance

text: About six million people lost power for roughly nine hours
as_written: some six million people without power for roughly nine hours
source: NASA and NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center accounts of the 1989 Quebec blackout

text: Explorer 1 discovered the radiation belts in 1958
as_written: In 1958 Explorer One discovered the radiation belts
source: Van Allen and Frank 1959, Nature; NASA

text: Magnetopause standoff distance scales as the cube root of the dipole moment
as_written: scales as the cube root of the field strength
source: Chapman-Ferraro pressure balance; Kivelson and Russell, Introduction to Space Physics

text: The typical sunward magnetopause distance is about 10 Earth radii
as_written: about ten Earth radii on the sunward side
source: Shue et al. 1997, Journal of Geophysical Research

text: Cube root of 1/7 gives about 0.5, so about 5 Earth radii
as_written: that falls to about five
source: Arithmetic from the cube-root scaling

text: Geostationary orbit is about 42,164 km from Earth's centre, about 6.6 Earth radii
as_written: about six and a half Earth radii
source: Standard orbital mechanics; Earth equatorial radius 6,378 km

text: The last full reversal, Brunhes-Matuyama, was about 770,000 years ago
as_written: about seven hundred and seventy thousand years ago
source: Singer 2014, Quaternary Science Reviews (773,000 years)

text: Laschamp excursion about 41,000 years ago, field about 5 percent of present, named for lava flows in France
as_written: roughly five percent of today's
source: Laj et al. 2014; Cooper et al. 2021, Science 371, 811

text: Cooper, Turney and colleagues proposed the Adams Event about 42,000 years ago coincided with a global environmental crisis; this is disputed
as_written: around forty-two thousand years ago
source: Cooper et al. 2021, Science 371, 811-818

text: The atmosphere above each square centimetre weighs about 1 kg, equivalent to about 10 m of water
as_written: weighs about one kilogram, which stops radiation about as well as ten metres of water
source: Standard atmosphere, 101,325 Pa / g; water-equivalent shielding of about 10 m

text: Cosmic rays contribute about 0.39 mSv per year of a roughly 2.4 mSv natural background
as_written: about four tenths of a millisievert a year, out of roughly two point four
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Report, Annex B

text: Past field collapses are not clearly linked to large ground-level radiation increases
as_written: reviews of past field collapses find the rise at ground level modest
source: Glassmeier and Vogt 2010, Space Science Reviews 155, 387-410

text: Typical solar wind speed is about 400 km/s
as_written: typically around four hundred kilometres per second
source: NASA Solar Wind fact sheet; NOAA SWPC

text: Mars lost its global dynamo roughly 4 billion years ago
as_written: roughly four billion years ago
source: Acuna et al. 1999, Science 284, 790; Lillis et al. 2008

text: Mars surface pressure is about 600 pascals, under 1 percent of Earth's
as_written: under one percent of Earth's
source: NASA Mars fact sheet

text: MAVEN measured Mars losing gas at about 100 grams per second
as_written: about a hundred grams every second
source: Jakosky et al. 2015, Science 350, aaa0210; NASA MAVEN

text: Mars Global Surveyor found strongly magnetised crustal patches in the late 1990s
as_written: In the late 1990s, Mars Global Surveyor found patches
source: Acuna et al. 1999, Science 284, 790

text: Magnetite Curie temperature is about 580 degrees Celsius
as_written: about five hundred and eighty degrees Celsius
source: Dunlop and Ozdemir, Rock Magnetism (1997)

text: Venus surface pressure is about 92 times Earth's
as_written: about ninety times ours
source: NASA Venus fact sheet

text: Ion escape rates at Earth, Mars and Venus are broadly similar
as_written: broadly similar
source: Gunell et al. 2018, Astronomy and Astrophysics 614, L3

text: Earth loses about 3 kg/s of hydrogen and 50 g/s of helium
as_written: about three kilograms of hydrogen and fifty grams of helium every second
source: Catling and Zahnle 2009, Scientific American, The Planetary Air Leak

text: Earth's oxygenated atmosphere is expected to last about 1.08 billion more years, plus or minus about 0.14
as_written: about one point oh eight billion years
source: Ozaki and Reinhard 2021, Nature Geoscience 14, 138-142
